minutes.headline: Water Commission delays a vote on a roughly $90,000 PFAS pilot study, awaiting DEP input before a special town meeting
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commission spent most of the meeting debating whether to fund a Tighe & Bond pilot study, priced around $86,000-$90,000, testing pH effects of combining Kings and Lancaster Ave. well water before PFAS treatment; commissioners and residents disagreed sharply over whether the study was necessary and whether Hickory Hills should be included, and the board deferred a special town meeting vote to the next meeting pending word from DEP. The board also covered ongoing Rolling Acres water main work, a MassDOT drainage/paving fix, an unresolved Woodlands kayak rack zoning violation, and early discussion of replacing an aging backhoe, with no purchases decided.

what_happened.line: The Water Commission put off scheduling a special town meeting vote on funding a PFAS pilot study, waiting on input from the state environmental agency.
The commission set up a follow-up meeting among the superintendent, the engineering firm and a resident who raised technical objections, before taking the study to the public.
Staff were directed to demand a written plan from Woodlands to remove kayak racks from a protected wellhead zone by the October 22 meeting.
The superintendent was asked to bring comparative cost figures for water main replacement work to the next meeting.
The board began weighing whether to replace an aging backhoe, tying that purchase to a future capital improvement plan rather than deciding now.

why_it_matters: A pilot study tied to PFAS treatment may require a special town meeting vote, meaning residents could be asked to approve new water district spending once cost and technical questions are resolved.
A protection-zone zoning violation near Hickory Hills remains unresolved, with a firm deadline now set for the responsible party to act.
Capital equipment and water main costs raised here signal future budget requests to the water district's ratepayers.
